**Summary:** PEP 621's exact title is **"Storing project metadata in pyproject.toml"** (Standards Track, Packaging, created 22-Jun-2020, Final). **Synthesis:**
- **Cargo.toml (the manifest)** — written by you; describes package metadata and dependencies "in a broad sense" via version *requirements* (e.g. `serde = "1.x"`), not exact pins.
- **Cargo.lock (the lockfile)** — contains "exact information about your dependencies"; it is "maintained by Cargo and should not be manually edited." It stores the resolver's output: "The result of the resolution is stored in the Cargo.lock file which 'locks' the dependencies to specific versions, and keeps them fixed over time" — covering the full graph (including transitive deps) with exact versions, sources, and checksums.
- **Why exact information?** Loose manifest ranges would re-resolve over time, so builds at different moments could pick different versions: "This would be bad because we want reproducible builds." Pinning exact versions makes every later build (CI, teammates, releases) identical, with changes happening only via manifest edits or explicit `cargo update` ("This command will update dependencies in the Cargo.lock file to the latest version"). Convention: "When in doubt, check Cargo.lock into the version control system (e.g. Git)."

**Answer:** RFC 9110's exact title is **"HTTP Semantics"** (also designated STD 97, published June 2022). It defines the version-independent semantics of HTTP — per its abstract: *"This document describes the overall architecture of HTTP, establishes common terminology, and defines aspects of the protocol that are shared by all versions,"* including core protocol elements, extensibility mechanisms, and the "http" and "https" URI schemes. It replaces the earlier HTTP/1.1 **RFC 7230–7235 (2014) family**: *"This document updates RFC 3864 and obsoletes RFCs 2818, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694, and portions of 7230"* (RFC 7234 went to RFC 9111 and the remaining 7230/7231 portions to RFC 9112).

**Public source:** https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc9110 (corroborated by the RFC Editor BibTeX record at https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9110)
